title: Bug Hunt Station 3 - Rocket Countdown (infinite loop)
body:
Goal: find out why the loop never ends, using a trace table.

  1. Open starter.py and press Run. The rocket never launches. After a moment the safety net stops the loop with a RuntimeError. (Without a safety net, you would press the red Stop button.)
  2. Make a trace table on paper. Follow the code line by line and write down the value of each variable every time round the loop:
round n numbers
1 5 [5]
2
3
  1. What should change every time round the loop, but never does? Fix it.

Done looks like:

5...
4...
3...
2...
1...
LIFT OFF!

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look at the while n > 0: line. The loop only stops when n is not more than 0. Fill in your trace table and watch what happens to n each round.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: A while loop needs something inside it that changes, or it can never end. Follow the code line by line and write down n after every round. Does n ever get smaller? Which lines inside the loop touch n?

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Your trace table should show n staying at 5 forever. The loop needs one new line inside it that updates n, with this shape: n = n ____ ____. Put it inside the loop, lined up with the other lines in the loop.

starter.name: starter.py
starter.raw:
# Bug Hunt Station 3: Rocket Countdown
# Press Run. The rocket never launches! After a moment you get a
# RuntimeError from the safety net. Make a trace table on paper:
#
#   round | n | numbers
#   ------+---+-----------
#     1   | 5 | [5]
#     2   |   |
#
# What should change each time round the loop... but does not?


def countdown(start):
    """Return a list counting down from start to 1, e.g. [3, 2, 1]."""
    numbers = []
    n = start
    rounds = 0
    while n > 0:
        numbers.append(n)
        rounds = rounds + 1
        if rounds > 1000:                  # safety net: you do not need to change this
            raise RuntimeError("The loop ran more than 1000 times. It looks stuck! Does n get smaller?")
    return numbers


def launch(start):
    """Print the countdown, then lift off."""
    for number in countdown(start):
        print(f"{number}...")
    print("LIFT OFF!")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    launch(5)
